title: Privacy-safe event journal and provenance chain

record.canonicalization: UTF-8 JSON, sorted keys, compact separators, no trailing newline

ids.digest: sha256: followed by 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters

state_machine.first: session_started with sequence 1 and genesis predecessor
state_machine.terminal_rule: No record follows a terminal disposition
state_machine.replay: An operation_id may be retried only with byte-identical normalized input; return the original record
state_machine.interruption: interrupted is terminal in this journal; resumption requires a new session and chain

retention.max_records: Positive bounded integer supplied by the caller
retention.eviction: Oldest records are evicted after append; the first retained record keeps its predecessor digest as an anchor
retention.projection: A retained journal may expose only bounded counts, sequences, identifiers, dispositions, and digests

privacy.redaction: Before persistence, recursively remove forbidden keys and replace credential-like or private-path string values with [REDACTED]
privacy.public_projection: Never includes payload; it includes only safe identifiers, bounded integers, dispositions, and digests

failure_semantics.side_effects: The checker performs no network, provider, process, Git, Coordinator, AWQ, AWG, UI, or LLM operation

evidence.binding: exact Coordinator task revision and canonical specification digest

limitations: The standard-library model is an in-memory reference and does not provide fsync, locking, signing, or crash durability.
A digest binds canonical bytes but does not authenticate their producer or prove Coordinator truth.
Redaction is a bounded contract filter, not a general personal-data classifier; callers must not supply raw private material.
follow_up: AR-0018 may integrate durable supervision and Coordinator state.
AWQ remains authoritative for accepting projected evidence.
